h1: The 6 Best Rechargeable Bluetooth Trackers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 rechargeable Bluetooth trackers compared on charging method, battery life, network, water rating and form.
summary: The Pebblebee Clip 5 is the best rechargeable tracker, with a 130 dB siren, USB-C charging, up to 12 months per charge and support for Find My or Find Hub. The UGREEN Finder Duo is the cross-platform four-pack, the Chipolo CARD is the wallet pick, and the Ultrbeka is the iPhone wallet card rated IP68.
intro: Rechargeable trackers trade one chore for another. You stop buying coin cells, but you take on a charge, and a tracker with a dead battery is just a keyring ornament. The deciding question is how often you charge and how painful it is, which is why the charging method and the battery life claim matter more than any other spec in this group.

We ranked six rechargeable trackers from the listings: charging method, battery life per charge, network support, water rating, ring volume and form factor. Two are wallet cards that charge on a Qi pad, and the rest are tags with USB-C. Battery life claims are the maker's figures under favorable use, so expect less if the tag rings often.

products.name: Pebblebee Clip 5 Bluetooth Tracker
products.verdict: A USB-C tag with a 130 dB siren, up to 12 months per charge, IP66 and both major networks.
products.description:
The Pebblebee Clip 5 charges over USB-C, lasts up to 12 months per charge, sounds a 130 dB siren, carries an IP66 rating at 10 g and works with Find My or Find Hub.

It ranks first because it combines the loudest siren listed, a rugged rating and a once-a-year charge on a network of your choice. It beats the Chipolo Loop's 125 dB by 5 dB, though that is a small gap. The cost is $25-50, which is more than the iPhone-only four-packs.

Buy it if you want a loud, rugged tag you charge once a year. Skip it if you want the lowest price per tag. It is the benchmark for this group.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants one loud, rugged tag that charges over USB-C.
products.skipIf: You need several tags for the price.

products.name: UGREEN Finder Duo Air Tracker Tags 4 Pack
products.verdict: A four-pack that works with iPhone and Android, lasting 365 days per charge over USB-C.
products.description:
The UGREEN Finder Duo comes as a four-pack for iPhone and Android, using Find My or Find Hub, with 365 days per charge and USB-C charging.

It ranks second because four tags for a mixed household cut the cost per tag, and the 365 day claim matches the Pebblebee. It loses to the Pebblebee on siren and weather rating, which the listing does not state.

Buy it if your home mixes iPhone and Android and you need several tags. Skip it if you want a documented water rating. Its pack size makes it the cost-per-tag leader for a family.
products.skipIf: You want a rating for rain.

products.name: TECKNET Rechargeable Air Tracker Tags
products.verdict: An MFi tag, iOS only, with USB-C charging, IP67 waterproofing, a 100 dB alarm and a motion tamper alert.
products.description:
The TECKNET is MFi certified for Apple Find My only, charges over built-in USB-C, has an IP67 rating, a 100 dB alarm and a motion tamper alert.

It ranks third because IP67 handles brief immersion, which suits luggage and bikes, and it costs under $25. The alarm is quieter than the Pebblebee's 130 dB, and it is iPhone only.

Buy it if you have an iPhone and want rain-ready protection. Skip it if anyone uses Android. Treat the rating as a bonus when the bag is exposed to weather.
products.idealFor: iPhone owners who want a rechargeable tag for rain and luggage.

products.name: Chipolo CARD Wallet Tracker
products.verdict: A thin wallet card with Qi magnetic charging, up to 1 year per charge and Find My or Find Hub.
products.description:
The Chipolo CARD is a thin wallet card that charges on a Qi magnetic pad, lasts up to 1 year per charge, works with Find My or Find Hub and has a 2-year warranty.

It ranks fourth because the card form fits where a tag cannot, but the charging needs a Qi charger. It costs $25-50. It is not water rated on the listing.

Buy it if you lose your wallet and own a Qi charger. Skip it if you want a USB-C tag. Check that your charger fits before ordering.
products.skipIf: You do not own a Qi charger.

products.name: UGREEN FineTrack Air Tracker Tags 4 Pack
products.verdict: A four-pack, iOS only and Apple MFi, charging over USB-C for up to 12 months.
products.description:
The UGREEN FineTrack Air is an iOS-only, Apple MFi four-pack that charges over USB-C, lasts up to 12 months per charge and has a Lost Mode.

It ranks fifth because it is only for iPhones and lists no water rating or ring volume. Four tags in one pack is the draw for a family of iPhone users.

Buy it if every phone in the house is an iPhone. Skip it if someone uses Android. Charge all four on the same day to keep them in sync.
products.idealFor: All-iPhone households that want four tags.

products.name: Ultrbeka Wallet Tracker Card
products.verdict: An MFi wallet card with Qi wireless charging, IP68 waterproofing and separation alerts.
products.description:
The Ultrbeka is an Apple Find My wallet card, MFi, that charges on a Qi wireless pad, carries an IP68 rating and includes separation alerts.

It ranks last because it is card-shaped and iPhone only, with no listed battery life or ring volume. IP68 is the strongest water rating in the group, which suits a wallet that gets caught in rain.

Buy it if you want a rated-waterproof wallet card. Skip it if you want a known battery life. Charge it before a trip, not after.
products.idealFor: iPhone users who want a waterproof wallet card.

whatMatters.detail: USB-C is the common cable, while Qi magnetic charging needs a pad. A tag with a built-in USB-C port is easiest. Check the charging method on the listing, and confirm you own the right charger. A tag you can plug into a phone charger you already own saves buying new gear, which is the real reason USB-C wins for most people.

Makers state up to 12 months or 365 days per charge, but real life shortens with frequent ringing. Check the claim, and plan to charge when the app warns of low battery. The gap between a claim and real life comes from how often the tag rings, so frequent searches drain a battery sooner.

Find My is for iPhones, Find Hub is for Android, and some tags join both. Check the network on the listing, and avoid iOS-only tags if anyone in the family uses Android. A tag on the wrong network is the most common refund reason, so match it to every phone that will use the app.

IP66 resists heavy spray, IP67 survives brief immersion and IP68 handles longer immersion. Check the IP rating on the listing, and note that many tags state none. Rain and sweat reach a wallet or a bike tag, so a rating is worth a few dollars if the item travels.

A card fits a wallet and a tag fits a keyring. Cards usually charge by Qi pad. Check the form on the listing, and decide which item you lose most often. Choose a card if the wallet is the item that goes missing, and a tag if it is the keys.

faq.q: Do rechargeable trackers work with Android?
faq.a: The Pebblebee, UGREEN Finder Duo and Chipolo CARD support Find Hub for Android. The TECKNET, UGREEN FineTrack Air and Ultrbeka are iPhone only. A phone reminder is easier than remembering.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Forgetting to charge. A claim of up to 12 months per charge means you charge once a year, so set a calendar reminder when you first set the tag up. The Pebblebee adds the loudest siren for the cost.

faq.q: Is the Pebblebee worth it over the UGREEN Finder Duo?
faq.a: If volume and rating matter, yes. The Pebblebee has a 130 dB siren and IP66, while the Duo offers four tags and 365 days per charge. Wipe a card clean before charging.

faq.q: How do I charge a wallet card?
faq.a: Place the Chipolo CARD or Ultrbeka on a Qi pad. The Chipolo uses magnetic charging, so check alignment before leaving it. Wet ports corrode, so dry them first.

faq.q: How should I look after them?
faq.a: Keep the USB-C port dry and free of lint. Charge to full when the app warns of a low battery, rather than letting it drain. Crowded places give the best location updates.

faq.q: Do they work without a phone nearby?
faq.a: They rely on nearby phones in the network to report their position, so crowded areas work best. In remote places a tracker is less useful. Spare charge cycles are cheap compared with replacing a lost wallet.

finalTake: The Pebblebee Clip 5 Bluetooth Tracker is the best rechargeable tracker, with a 130 dB siren, IP66 rating and up to 12 months per charge. The UGREEN Finder Duo is the cross-platform pack, the Chipolo CARD is the wallet answer, and the TECKNET is the cheap rain-ready iPhone tag. Set a charging reminder.
